## Contents
- Identifying with the damping loop **closed**, using no controller model.
- How the reference-based FRF cancels the controller — see [closing the loop](../tutorial/closing-the-loop.qmd#identifying-in-closed-loop-controller-aware).

[![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/05-closed-loop-arm.ipynb)  ·  run this page live (no install; the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant)

The most realistic case: a suspension identified **with its damping loop closed**. The
feedback acts on the resonance being measured, so the instrument shows the
closed-loop response $T = P/(1+PC)$, whose peak is suppressed by the loop gain $1+PC$.
Fitting $T$ and calling it the plant is **biased**.

The Pintelon–Schoukens **reference-based FRF** — the ratio of period-averaged spectra
$\overline{Y}/\overline{X}$ off the drive monitor and the response — cancels the controller
automatically and returns the **open-loop plant directly**: no controller object, no
$1/(1-TC)$ division. We run the full diagnostic set with the loop genuinely closed in the
twin, and use `python-control` only to draw the suppressed $T$ for the bias story —
never in the fit.

Closed loop is a **first-class, declarable mode**: a config names the digital controller
`C(s)`, where the excitation is injected (before or after the controller), and the
after-controller **drive monitor** channel used as the FRF input — so the same campaign runs
straight from `SysIDLoop` / the CLI ([§ run it as a declared campaign](#run-it-as-a-declared-campaign)).

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Setup — imports, house plot style, plant, controller, prior"
import sys, pathlib
_p = pathlib.Path.cwd()
for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]:
    for _d in (_c, _c / "docs"):
        if (_d / "sysid_plots.py").exists() and str(_d) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(_d))

import numpy as np
import control as ct
import sysid_plots as sp
from sysid_campaign import run_siso_passes, param_sigmas, param_convergence_series

from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant
from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance
from system_ident.design.pintelon import prior_robust_excitation

FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 4096, 6           # T_fft = 128 s (> 3/f_min), df ≈ 0.008 Hz
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS
ACT_LIMIT = 1000.0

P_TRUE = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)], 100.0)        # true open-loop plant
prior  = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.3, 14.0)], 130.0)        # ~30% off in f0 and Q

k, wc = 2e-3, 2 * np.pi * 12.0                                # velocity-damping C(s)
C = ([k, 0.0], [1.0 / wc, 1.0])

tw = TwinBackend(SuspensionPlant({"POS": P_TRUE}, FS),
                 {"C1:EXC": "POS"}, {"C1:RSP": "POS"}, fs=FS,
                 sensor_asd=1e-4, disturbance_asd=1e-4, controllers={"POS": C}, seed=3)

f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band  = (f_all >= 0.1) & (f_all <= 5.0)
freq  = f_all[band]
Pyy, Px_tot = np.ones_like(freq), 1.0
```

## The parameters we're chasing

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Prior vs true open-loop parameters"
f0t, Qt = sp.f0_q(P_TRUE); f0p, Qp = sp.f0_q(prior)
sp.param_table(
    ["", "f₀ [Hz]", "Q", "DC gain |G(0)|"],
    [["prior", f"{f0p:.4f}", f"{Qp:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}"],
     ["true open-loop", f"{f0t:.4f}", f"{Qt:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(P_TRUE):.4g}"]],
    caption="Before measuring")
```

## 1 — Design the excitation

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Prior-robust drive; variance win vs flat"
Pxx_opt  = prior_robust_excitation(freq, prior, Pyy, Px_tot, 0.5, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, P_TRUE, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, TOTAL)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, P_TRUE, Pxx_flat, Pyy, TOTAL)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

sp.excitation_design(
    freq, np.abs(P_TRUE.eval(freq)), np.sqrt(Pxx_opt), np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    prior_mag=np.abs(prior.eval(freq)), ratio=ratio,
    annotations=[(1.0, "f₀ = 1.0 Hz, Q = 20")]).show()
```

## 2 — Run the campaign (loop closed)

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Run 3 passes through the closed loop"
hist = run_siso_passes(tw, "C1:EXC", "C1:RSP", prior, fs=FS, nperseg=NPERSEG,
                       n_periods=N_PERIODS, band=band, freq=freq, Pyy=Pyy,
                       px_total=Px_tot, n_passes=3, prior_uncertainty=0.5, seed=0)
final = hist[-1]["model"]    # already the OPEN-LOOP plant — the loop is cancelled
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Parameter evolution: prior → each pass → true"
rows = [["prior", f"{f0p:.4f}", f"{Qp:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}", "—"]]
for h in hist:
    f0, Q = sp.f0_q(h["model"])
    rows.append([f"pass {h['pass']}", f"{f0:.4f}", f"{Q:.2f}",
                 f"{sp.dc_gain(h['model']):.4g}", f"{h['frac']:.2e}"])
rows.append(["true", f"{f0t:.4f}", f"{Qt:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(P_TRUE):.4g}", "—"])
sp.param_table(["step", "f₀ [Hz]", "Q", "DC gain |G(0)|", "σ/θ (CRB)"], rows,
               caption="Parameters at each step (recovered with no controller-division)")
```

## Run it as a declared campaign {#run-it-as-a-declared-campaign}

The closed loop is **declarable** — no ad-hoc driver code. A config names the controller
`C(s)`, the `injection_point`, and the after-controller `drive` channel; `SysIDLoop` reads
that drive monitor as the FRF input X and recovers the open-loop plant. This is exactly what
`system_ident run configs/closed_loop_demo.yml --twin` executes.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Declare the closed loop in a config and run SysIDLoop"
from system_ident.config import RunConfig
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop as _Loop

cfg = {
  "run": {"name": "cl", "excitation_mode": "sequential"},
  "channels": {"excitation": {"POS": "C1:EXC"}, "readback": {"POS": "C1:RSP"},
               "drive": {"POS": "C1:DRV"}},        # after-controller drive monitor → X
  "measurement": {"fs": FS, "freq_min": 0.1, "freq_max": 5.0,
                  "segment_duration": NPERSEG / FS, "n_segments": N_PERIODS, "px_total": 1.0},
  "strategy": {"estimator": "gml", "input_designer": "pintelon_schoukens", "n_design_iter": 3},
  "twin": {"sensor_asd": 1e-4, "disturbance_asd": 1e-4,
           "plant": {"POS": {"resonances": [[1.0, 20]], "gain": 100}},
           "controllers": {"POS": {"num": [k, 0.0], "den": [1.0 / wc, 1.0]}},
           "injection_point": "after_controller"},  # or "before_controller"
  "priors": {"POS": {"resonances": [[1.3, 14]], "gain": 130}},
  "safety": {"actuator_sat": 1e6, "rms_ceiling": {"POS": 1e6}, "ramp_down_secs": 2.0},
  "stop_criteria": {"uncertainty_target": 0.02, "max_iter": 3},
}
rc = RunConfig(raw=cfg)
backend = rc.build_twin_backend(seed=0)
res = _Loop(backend, rc.build_estimator(), rc.build_designer(),
            rc.build_watchdog(backend)).run(rc.raw, rc.build_priors(), seed=0)
f0_cfg, q_cfg = sp.f0_q(res.models["POS"])
print(f"config-driven closed-loop fit:  f0 = {f0_cfg:.3f} Hz, Q = {q_cfg:.1f}"
      f"   (true open-loop: 1.000 Hz, 20.0 — no controller-division)")
```

## 3 — Is the drive gentle? The measurement time series

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive monitor + response, first ~64 s of pass 1"
t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
sp.timeseries(
    t, [("drive monitor (actuator signal)", hist[0]["drive"], sp.SKY)],
    [("response (damped by the loop)", hist[0]["response"], sp.GOLD)],
    titles=["<b>Drive monitor</b> — actuator signal (Schroeder multisine, loop closed)",
            "<b>Response</b> — suspension motion (suppressed by the damping loop)"]).show()
```

## 4 — Bode: the bias story, magnitude / phase / coherence

The closed-loop $T$ (grey dotted) has a **suppressed** resonance — fitting it would
understate the plant. The reference-based measurement (grey points) instead lands on the
true open-loop $P$, and the fit recovers it.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Draw the suppressed T, then the full Bode stack"
P_ct = ct.tf(list(P_TRUE.num), list(P_TRUE.den))
T_ct = ct.minreal(ct.feedback(P_ct, ct.tf(*C)))
T_model = TFModel(num=np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ct.tf(T_ct).num[0][0], float)),
                  den=np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ct.tf(T_ct).den[0][0], float)))

mask = hist[-1]["mask"]
sp.bode(freq, [
    dict(name="true open-loop P",      H=P_TRUE.eval(freq),  color=sp.SKY, width=2.8),
    dict(name="closed-loop T (biased)", H=T_model.eval(freq), color=sp.GRAY, dash="dot"),
    dict(name="measured (±σ, open-loop)", H=hist[-1]["H_acc"], color="#5B6B7B",
         mode="markers", err=hist[-1]["err_acc"], mask=mask),
    dict(name="ML fit P̂",              H=final.eval(freq),   color=sp.GOLD, dash="dash"),
], coh=hist[-1]["coh"], coh_mask=mask).show()
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The bias is cancelled, not corrected
Near 1 Hz the loop suppresses the closed-loop peak by $1+PC$. The old remedy measured $T$
and divided the controller back out by hand. Here the reference-based ratio-of-averages
**cancels the loop in the measurement itself** — the grey points already lie on $P$, so
$\hat P$ is unbiased without ever naming $C$ in the fit. At LIGO, where control gain can be
40 dB near a pendulum resonance, cancelling at the measurement is far more robust than a
post-hoc division.
:::

## 5 — Fit residuals

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Normalized residual + histogram"
resid = ((hist[-1]["H_acc"] - final.eval(freq)) / hist[-1]["err_acc"]).real
sp.residuals(freq, resid, mask).show()
```

## 6 — Parameter recovery against the Cramér–Rao bound

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Parameter recovery with CRB error bars"
f0f, Qf = sp.f0_q(final)
sig = param_sigmas(final, hist[-1]["cov"])
sp.parameter_recovery([
    dict(label="f₀ [Hz]",        prior=f0p, fit=f0f, true=f0t, sigma=sig["f0"]),
    dict(label="Q",              prior=Qp,  fit=Qf,  true=Qt,  sigma=sig["Q"]),
    dict(label="DC gain |G(0)|", prior=sp.dc_gain(prior), fit=sp.dc_gain(final),
         true=sp.dc_gain(P_TRUE), sigma=sig["gain"], log=True),
]).show()
print(f"recovered open-loop P̂:  f0 = {f0f:.3f} Hz, Q = {Qf:.1f}  (no controller-division)")
```

## 7 — Drive-safety margins

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive peak & RMS vs the actuator limit, per pass"
sp.saturation([{"pass": h["pass"], "peak": h["peak"], "rms": h["rms"]} for h in hist],
              limit=ACT_LIMIT).show()
```

## 8 — Convergence — every parameter

```{python}
#| code-summary: "σᵢ/θᵢ vs pass, per parameter"
sp.convergence(param_convergence_series(hist, ["f0", "Q", "gain"], ["f₀", "Q", "gain"]),
               target=0.05).show()
```

## 9 — Pass-by-pass: the measurement sharpening

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Measured FRF + fit, overlaid per pass"
sp.pass_overlay(freq,
    [dict(meas_mag=np.abs(h["H"]), fit_mag=np.abs(h["model"].eval(freq)),
          mask=h["mask"]) for h in hist],
    np.abs(P_TRUE.eval(freq))).show()
```
